name: Sporobolus

project_scope.note: Current manifest contains all three canonical species. S. compositus species-rank card is PASS (Hays, Bexar, Kerr), while disputed variety-level/Travis records are excluded from that determination. Historical B149 HOLD text below is retained as historical context, not current admission status.

priority: rooted annual or persistent perennial crown
complete terminal panicle with true side branches
upper sheath / potential concealed flowers (not exclusive)
mature one-flowered glumes, lemma and mm scale
400× compound microscope lemma surface for disputed material
study_strategy.warning: Head contraction, height and presence of upper-sheath self-pollinating flowers all overlap. Mature, fresh seed and real microscope images are critical for exact separation; protect the three existing canonical species and unresolved variety disputes.

comparison_lesson.title: Three Central Texas dropseeds — first learn the head, then test the tough pair
comparison_lesson.memory_rule: ROOT → HEAD → SHEATH → SPIKELET → SEED / LEMMA. When in doubt, record Sporobolus sp.
quick_split: S. clandestinus (rough dropseed): perennial with narrow, strongly contracted head; compare its mature lemma and usually non-gelatinizing, non-separating pericarp on freshly wetted ripe grain against S. compositus.

S. compositus (composite dropseed): perennial, often longer crowded head; can resemble S. clandestinus closely. Fresh ripe grain pericarp tends to gelatinize/separate when wetted; old grains may fail. Species-rank learner card is already canonical; variety-level debates remain unresolved.

S. vaginiflorus (poverty dropseed): generally smaller annual with thin leaves and often terminal and axillary concealed flowering; rooted base + mature reproductive detail needed. Hidden sheath flowers are not an exclusive diagnostic.
guardrails: Do not identify S. clandestinus versus S. compositus from head length alone. Documented expert herbarium conflicts exist in Central Texas.
Multiple related dropseeds produce cleistogamous flowers concealed in sheaths; the presence of such flowers does not prove S. vaginiflorus.
The moist pericarp response works best with fresh mature seed; reaction on old collections may be incomplete or delayed.
Fine lemma hooks, prickles and silica cells are compound microscope characters (roughly 400×). Do not annotate them on phone photographs.
Native/county status is preserved and not re-reviewed. Three canonical species only; keep historical variety-level source disputes separate.
field_photo_steps: Photograph entire rooted plant at base, showing any persistent crown and old culm remains; pair with habitat view.
Hold true panicle upright with a millimeter ruler; capture narrow branch positions AND spikelet-bearing side.
Lift upper sheath gently and document any actually visible enclosed axillary flower, not a generic leaf collar.
Pick ripe one-flowered unawned spikelet; photograph outer glumes and inner fertile lemma at measured magnification.
For difficult mature perennial IDs, test a FRESH ripe grain in a water drop with timed photos, or consult the microscope / voucher.

look_here_first: DROPSEED FIELD KEY: (1) check a rooted base (perennial S. clandestinus and S. compositus versus annual S. vaginiflorus); (2) photograph the entire contracted PANICLE; (3) inspect upper LEAF SHEATHS, but know multiple species can have concealed self-pollinated flowers; (4) dissect a mature single-flowered, unawned spikelet; (5) separate hard perennial look-alikes by mature LEMMA and fresh grain pericarp, not panicle shape alone.

shared_structure_examples.plain_english: The branching flower/seed head at the top of the grass.
shared_structure_examples.look_for: Branch length, angle and how closely the spikelets crowd the axis.
shared_structure_examples.why_it_matters: Separates the short contracted heads of poverty/rough dropseed from the often longer compositus head; head openness overlaps.

shared_structure_examples.plain_english: Tiny flowering unit, outer bracts and bract around its flower.
shared_structure_examples.look_for: Detach a mature one-flowered, usually awnless spikelet; separate outer glumes and fertile lemma. Scan lemma at 400× for hooks/prickles when needed.
shared_structure_examples.why_it_matters: Separates Sporobolus from multi-flowered lookalikes; character-level S. compositus and S. clandestinus separation needs fresh seed/microscopy.

shared_structure_examples.plain_english: The leaf tube around the stem; some hidden self-pollinating flowers develop inside.
shared_structure_examples.look_for: Examine upper sheaths of all three species for possible axillary, self-pollinating florets. Show the SHEATH OPENING and flower together.
shared_structure_examples.why_it_matters: Especially worth photographing on S. vaginiflorus, but not exclusive to that species or sufficient for identification.

shared_structure_examples.plain_english: The lower grass stem and persistent tuft or annual root system.
shared_structure_examples.look_for: Whether old perennial tillers persist at the crown or an annual plant roots from a single season.
shared_structure_examples.why_it_matters: First division between S. vaginiflorus and the two perennial species.

shared_structure_examples.plain_english: Seed coat surrounding a mature grain, sometimes swelling and coming away in water.
shared_structure_examples.look_for: Photograph fresh dry grain, then the same grain after a timed water drop under magnification; retain specimen ID.
shared_structure_examples.why_it_matters: Useful when the perennial rough and composite dropseed pair overlap: compositus generally gelatinizes and separates, clandestinus generally does not. Old grains are unreliable.

genus_diagnostics.genus_recognition: Grasses with small spikelets in a panicle and dropseed-type grains. Recognize grass anatomy first: culm nodes, sheath, ligule and spikelets; no single panicle silhouette confirms genus.

confusable_genera.distinction: Also fine-panicled grasses; dissect spikelet glumes/lemmas and mature fruit rather than relying on cloudlike heads.
Usually multiple florets per spikelet; compare an entire dissected spikelet against Sporobolus, where spikelets are generally one-flowered.

visual_comparison.title: Sporobolus — 3 species, real rough-dropseed spikelet/seed, poverty-dropseed sheath and composite varieties
visual_comparison.subtitle: Eleven new actual Bob Harms rough-dropseed regional teaching images expand prior composite var. drummondii/macer and poverty-dropseed lessons. Fine lemma 400× prickles and wet-grain micro are authentic separate research references, not publicly copied panels. Eleven rough-dropseed Harms photo panels now backed by real source JPEGs without duplicating image bytes. Eight original composite-dropseed varietal photos are now physically archived, with variety-specific attribution and no invented macro arrows.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: ROUGH (*S. clandestinus*) = perennial narrow panicle, actual SEPARATE one-floret grain, ligule short HAIR FRINGE; reliable vs composite requires non-GELATINIZING pericarp + 400× PRICKLES. COMPOSITE = perennial, mature grain pericarp typically gelatinizes/slips off. POVERTY = mostly small annual-like with terminal and upper-sheath flowering. Each needs source-vouchered rooted plants.

Gross habit/flowering structure arrows verified from existing real JPG pixels. Each original creator and photo license retained. No claims of microscope-visible hooks, pericarp swelling or hidden flowers from these pictures. Source-determined IDs remain provisional until diagnostic specimens.
2026-10-22: eight authentic exact-species Bob Harms original SPVA-a3,b1,c,i,J1,j2,d,L Central Texas source photos individually visually opened and their source pages credit checked. They add a truly rooted plant, upper culm/sheath and two flowering positions, a narrow flowering head with dark purplish exserted structures, source-scaled mature spikelet bracts, disarticulation plate and ciliate ligule zone. © Bob Harms author grants original educational/scientific use with credited name, NOT CC. Eight EXTERNAL links, no new archived JPEG files, no new unsupported individual microscope pixel arrows. Conservatively teach leaf sheath vs ligule only, selfing flowers not photographed enclosed and 400× hook/cell sculpture unresolved. Preserve existing 6 other source panels and their visible source annotations and original rights, no nativity/taxon/range changes. Pending 2026-10-22 local fresh Hays rooted same-specimen and actual microscopic keyed detail.
2026-10-22: authentic original Bob Harms Selected Central Texas Monocots variety-qualified source photo set: S. compositus var. drummondii (SPCOD3-b,i,J0,J1,v) and var. macer (SPCOM-b,j1,8). All eight actual JPEGs checked at source; external remote original images only, source copyright © Bob Harms reusable for credited scientific/educational public lesson NOT CC. Original three-part author's SPCOD3-v has DRUMMONDII in left and middle panels but DIFFERENT species S. CLANDESTINUS on right. SPCOM-8 horizontal linked rhizome photographed with scale shows only var. MACER, cannot imply all S. compositus forms have runners. Original nearby two source single-species images and 8 previous S. vaginiflorus remote examples and other genus media unchanged, original arrows retained, none newly fabricated. Author-reported 2002/2014 TEX/LL mixed determinations: closeout requires preserved taxonomy/range hold, glume lengths, mature grain wet pericarp and lemma-surface microscopy. Exact localized photo voucher uncertain, not Hays-proven.
2026-10-22 rough-dropseed authentic eleven original Bob Harms Central Texas photo plates SPCL-a,a1,b,I,i1,I2,J,J1,J2,S,L added and individually original-photo visually reviewed. These exact source labels show flowering exserted reddish anthers, one-floret spikelet plus loose cream-colored grains, developing and mature contracted panicles, and a source-calibrated blade/sheath junction whose ~0.2–0.3mm HAIR LIGULE cannot be fine-arrow targeted from this resolution. Copyright Bob Harms; original author grants science/education-use with attribution for Selected Central Texas Monocots, NOT Creative Commons. Eleven new images externally linked only; no new JPG binary files or speculative micro arrows. Original 22 genus panels retained, as well as all 6 original local stored species files/old gross arrows and earlier compositus/vaginiflorus source anatomy. Research source separate SPORO actual 20/36 min wet pericarp and 100/400× rough prickle photomicrographs was FOUND (Harms), but NOT embedded because individual image republication grant for distinct SPORO subsite was not established by Selected Monocots license. Two study page links may be followed. Pericarp not necessarily an absolute binary, particularly old dry vouchers. No changes to taxonomy or native by county.
